subject.title: fix(plugins): allow user-installed and generated plugins to use api.runtime.state

question: Which plugin provenance or operator action should permanently authorize access to persistent `api.runtime.state` stores and ingress queues?
rationale: The existing API deliberately restricts these helpers, while the proposed origin-based exception and the linked `load-path` failure expose multiple plausible trust models; code inspection cannot choose the intended security and compatibility contract.

options.title: Use explicit operator trust
options.body: Centralize authorization around a durable install-policy or explicit operator-trust fact that can cover managed installs, enabled workspace plugins, generated plugins, and approved load paths consistently.

options.title: Trust selected origins
options.body: Accept global and workspace origins as sufficient trust while leaving load-path and other origins behind the existing gate, with documentation explaining the distinction.

options.title: Keep the existing gate
options.body: Retain bundled and trusted-official access only, and change plugin generation or installation so qualifying local plugins receive the existing trusted-install provenance.

recommendation.title: Use explicit operator trust
recommendation.body: Centralize authorization around a durable install-policy or explicit operator-trust fact that can cover managed installs, enabled workspace plugins, generated plugins, and approved load paths consistently.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the plugin state API and are the strongest available history signal for its intended trust model.
